name: Valkey Rebuild and Recovery Protocol
description: Implement the rebuild-on-start protocol: on every cold start, scan PGlite for non-terminal work items, unclosed attempts, pending scheduled obligations, and unacknowledged work — then repopulate Valkey queues, sorted sets, and heartbeat state. Must run in under 1 second, be idempotent, and derive all state from PGlite — no inventing state, no double-enqueuing terminal work, no acknowledging unknown stream entries. The current manual rebuild is a scaffold; this mission closes only when PGlite is the rebuild authority.
purpose: Valkey loss must be annoying, not catastrophic. After a Valkey wipe or process restart, the system can rebuild non-terminal scheduled/enqueued/retryable work from PGlite without inventing state, double-enqueuing terminal work, or acknowledging unknown stream entries. The rebuild protocol is a normal operational path that runs on every cold start, not a disaster recovery drill.
acceptanceCriteria: Rebuild runs on every cold start where Valkey process is not running
Completes in under 1 second for typical state
Idempotent: running twice produces same Valkey projection derived from PGlite
Scans non-terminal PGlite rows only — never rebuilds completed, failed-terminal, cancelled, or dead-lettered work
Emits recovery receipts for every rebuild action
Handles all wipe scenarios: no persistence, deleted app support dir, migration, dev reset, crash before AOF fsync
History never lost — only seconds of coordination progress may be lost
